display_name: 7E-2E — durable learning events and verified commits
implementation_state: The journal is durable, ordered, and fail-closed, its corruption handling is sound, and the idempotency defect found at revalidation has been repaired: the duplicate check now compares the bytes the incoming record would be written as against the bytes already on disk, so a byte-identical retry is a duplicate even when a float does not survive a JSON round trip. All required gates hold.
unblock_condition: Satisfied. All four required gates hold: durability, ordering, idempotency and sequence semantics, verified commit lineage, and replay closure. Idempotency is established by byte comparison against the stored frame, with a regression test that reproduces the original refusal when the fix is reverted.
notes: A type-level LearningEvent is no longer a process-local value. The accepted event type is journalled as-is and no second event type was introduced; model_identity.rs was not modified.

REPAIRED, E-089: each scanned frame now retains its body exactly as it appears on disk, and the duplicate check compares the bytes the incoming record WOULD be written as against those bytes, so the comparison never passes through a float parser. The two volatile wall-clock fields, recorded_at and event.created_at, are substituted with the stored record's own values first, which preserves the contract that a retry re-creating the same event at a different instant is still the same event. The new test reproduces the exact IdempotencyConflict on sequence 1 when only the source fix is reverted, and covers all three directions: unchanged retry is a duplicate, later-instant retry is a duplicate, and a genuinely changed record is still refused and writes nothing.

ACCEPTED COSTS of the byte comparison, stated rather than left implicit: a scan now holds each raw body alongside the parsed one, which at the bounded record count roughly doubles body memory; and the comparison depends on a stable serializer byte form, which the pinned serde_json gives inside this repository but a log written by a different serializer version could disagree with. The comparison is also STRICTER than the field comparison it replaced, so a field added later that turns out to be volatile now fails safe instead of silently ignored.

The write path cannot be reached with a foreign schema version, because both record constructors hardcode the current version and the scan already refuses another one. So making the comparison exact over the whole body changed no legitimate caller's outcome.

CONSTRAINT CARRIED FORWARD TO 7E-2F: the journal is append-only and last-write-wins is refused, so an event recorded before it was applied cannot be updated in place to add its result commit. An applied event is a NEW record, and activation is designed around that rather than around mutation.

A prefix of a valid log is itself a valid log, so no per-record checksum can detect a suffix removed at a frame boundary. The completion anchor exists for that case alone: record count, next sequence, log length, whole-log checksum, tail frame checksum, and its own checksum, written after the log is flushed and renamed into place.

The frame checksum chains its predecessor, which is what makes a removed or reordered INTERIOR frame detectable independently of the sequence check. It is deliberately public, because a durable format only its own writer can verify is not a durable format.
FNV-1a-64 is an accidental-corruption checksum, not a MAC, and the module says so. The real integrity witness is the content-addressed CommitId.

The portable create_new lock can be left stale by a process that dies without unwinding, and the module does not claim otherwise. The format is the safety net: chained checksums plus a monotonic sequence turn interleaved or duplicate writes into a loud typed refusal rather than silent loss. Concurrent writers are refused, not merged, because choosing which of two records claiming one sequence came first IS last-write-wins.

Anti-degradation is an exact assertion, not a comment: every canonical sample is validated with the accepted validator, projected through into_legacy, and the projection must equal the event's samples exactly, on the way in and again on the way out. The lossy path still exists because the accepted event type is this node's subject, so it is labelled LegacyProjection, the label is derived rather than supplied, the degradation text lives in the log bytes, and JournalRecord::is_degraded() is on the record.
The process-local evt-<n> id form is refused as VolatileEventId, because a dedup key that restarts in every process is not a durable identity.

The anchor's post-rename directory flush is #[cfg(unix)] because std offers none on Windows. The documented consequence is that a lost anchor can only cause a NotAJournal refusal, never a silently accepted truncated log.

Opening this journal cannot train, activate, or schedule anything. read_records is the only way to obtain a record, it is an explicit call, and it returns records rather than a model, checkpoint, or update.
